chunks: From him, from Al-Hasan ibn Ali (peace be upon him), who said:

I asked Abu Al-Hasan (peace be upon him) about a man who bought a barren land from another man for one hundred kurrs of wheat, on the condition that he give him from the land. He said, 'It is forbidden.' I said, 'May I be your ransom, for I buy the land with a known measure of wheat and barley from each other.' He said, 'There is no objection to that.'

key_terms.جُعِلْتُ فِدَاكَ: May I be your ransom (a phrase of respect)
key_terms.كُرٍّ: A unit of volume/measure for grain
key_terms.لَا بَأْسَ: There is no objection / It is permissible

ai.seo_question: What is the difference between a forbidden and permissible land sale involving payment in grain?
ai.summary: This hadith from Imam al-Rida (AS) clarifies the distinction between *bay' al-jurba* (sale of unknown quantity) and permissible commodity exchange by contrasting a single-commodity payment sourced from the land itself with a multi-commodity barter. It highlights the Shia juristic principle that uncertainty (*gharar*) in the source or quantity of the payment renders the transaction void, whereas known measures of distinct commodities ensure validity. This ruling is foundational in *fiqh al-mu'amalat* for validating trade contracts involving agricultural produce.
